questions.q: What are the two income streams a yield farm stacks together?
options: LP trading fees (real revenue) and emission rewards (newly minted protocol tokens)
Only trading fees -- yield farms don't emit tokens
questions.explain: A yield farm pays LP trading fees plus newly emitted reward tokens on top, which is why the two have very different risk profiles.

questions.q: A farm emits $2,000,000/year in reward value into a pool with $10,000,000 TVL. What is the farm APY by this lesson's formula?

options: Capital locked permanently by a vesting contract
Capital that can only be used for governance voting
Liquidity that moves purely to chase the highest current yield, with no loyalty to the protocol
questions.explain: Mercenary capital arrives when emissions start and leaves the moment a competing farm offers a better rate, taking liquidity depth with it.

questions.q: Why can a farm's advertised APY fall even if the emission rate itself hasn't changed?
options: APY is fixed by smart contract and can never change
Because the reward token's price can drop under sell pressure, reducing the USD value of the same token emission
TVL has no effect on APY
Advertised APY only changes once per year
questions.explain: The APY formula uses the reward's USD value; if farmers sell the reward and its price falls, the same token emission is worth less, so the effective APY falls.

questions.q: Which design choice helps prevent farmers from dumping rewards the instant they're credited?
options: Vesting reward claims over weeks or months instead of paying out instantly
Removing all trading fees from the pool
questions.explain: Vesting reward claims linearly over time, rather than instant payout, is one of the main levers against immediate sell pressure.
